basis: Printed SchmidtKaulp262item66 has grease miŋ, p267item105 has sunny slope nʲin myṣ; raw min merged dissimilar source forms and meanings.

branches.analysis: Fat/grease miŋ plausibly continues mēdas through contraction and nasalization; no stress is marked.
Two-word spatial expression, likely Tibetan/Purik day/sun-related first component, not mēdas fat. Donor phrase and morphology remain open.

basis: Printed SchmidtKaulp264item81 village bun differs from p279item263 we beŋ/bɜɜ. DB ben collapses them.

branches.analysis: Settlement term homophonous with field bun; a field-to-settlement extension is possible, but ultimate vāpana or other ancestry is not established.
Nasalized/final-nasal first-person plural variant in the vayam/be paradigm, unmarked. Other bɜɜ alternative has its own raw record.

basis: Printed SchmidtKaulp265item97 day dis and p273item182 give dis are separate homonyms; sun/day suri has a separate raw record.

branches.analysis: Day noun belongs to divasa/day family; unmarked monosyllable, separate from giving verb.
Giving root dā plus recurring s citation morphology; no stress marked. Not a continuation of day divasa.

basis: Printed SchmidtKaulp275item209 has 'apo, kʲii. Superscript j is palatalization, not stress; whole raw string reverses alternatives.

branches.analysis: Álpa-derived adjective after lp simplification with final o; initial short syllable stress. Brokskat does not show Gilgit's long taáto-type mora contrast here.
Palatalized-k quantity word, potentially an interrogative/indefinite derivative, but no secure old formation is known. It is unmarked for stress, contrary to an earlier tentative k'ii reading.

basis: Printed SchmidtKaulp276item215 has two full adjectives, 'punjis and pe'ree, with distinct stress positions.

branches.analysis: Initial-stressed punjis may be a filled/result form, but the nj/is morphology needs source grammar before a pūrṇa/pūraya assignment.

Final-stressed peree may belong to the pūr filling family, with an extended final ee formation; donor/derivation remains unverified. It cannot be pooled with punjis to create a multiple-stress lexical item.

basis: Printed SchmidtKaulp276item220 has ṭhaa, ṭhan'yaa as alternatives, not a single predicative phrase.

branches.analysis: Long unmarked monosyllabic hunger term; comparison with thirst/hunger roots requires independent evidence.
Final-stressed extended hunger adjective, perhaps related to ṭhaa by n/yaa derivation; this morphology is a plausible source of accent difference but not an established historical reconstruction.

basis: Printed SchmidtKaulp269item129 lists zo and laŋ'to as alternatives; sourcep248 identifies both as Purik loans.

branches.analysis: Purik animal term, unmarked.
Purik bull term, final stress; loan-adaptation evidence only.

basis: Printed SchmidtKaulp272item163 lists chah, mak'kii; distinct maize names, not compound.

branches.analysis: Explicit Purik loan per sourcep248, unmarked.
Regional makai maize word, final stress. Family9879 is only the existing comparative grouping; no direct derivation from markaka bird is accepted.

basis: Printed SchmidtKaulp277item237 lists 'titaq, 'sææno; two loan alternatives with initial stress.

branches.analysis: Purik small adjective per sourcep248, initial stress.
Unidentified Indo-Aryan loan per sourcep248, initial stress on long front vowel; exact quality approximate.

basis: Ushojo survey entry has slash-separated joŋ / pɑ̃ leg; these are distinct lexical stems.

branches.analysis: Candidate jaṅghā lower leg through medial aspiration/final-vowel loss and rounding; full Turner and regional evidence still required before a new research family.
Pā́da foot/leg with intervocalic d loss and contraction, unmarked short/nasal vowel.

basis: Ushojo survey entry gives cical / xata mud, two lexical alternatives with initial stress.

branches.analysis: Kicca/cical mud word with final l formation, initially stressed.
Separate xata soil/filth word; possible regional borrowing remains unresolved. Initial stress is independent of cical.

basis: Ushojo survey sheep entry explicitly distinguishes female ili and male miṇḍal, separate stems.

branches.analysis: Likely ēḍa/eḍi sheep family with retroflex-to-l outcome; no stress is marked in the female token.
Mēṇḍha ram root with al extension and final stress. Formation differs independently from the female sheep noun.

basis: Ushojo survey horse entry explicitly gives feminine ašpi and masculine ašpo, both initially stressed.

branches.analysis: Áśva horse root plus feminine i cell, initial stress; gender alternation independently specified.
Áśva horse root plus masculine o cell, initial stress. Same family as feminine, not independent etymon confirmation.
